title: Look after health when help is far away
short: Medicines, a first aid kit, stress, children, people who need care
intro: Readings for looking after health when doctors and pharmacies are hard to reach: medicines and a home pharmacy, fear and stress after a disaster, children in a crisis, and people who need extra care. For injuries and sudden illness, see the first aid guide.

choices.label: Enough medicines, and a home pharmacy
choices.hint: Regular medicines, prescriptions, keeping them safe

read.label: A home pharmacy and medicines for ten days
read.note: In German. Doctors and pharmacies may be out of reach; what to keep at home, and why a first aid course helps.

read.label: Where and how to keep medicines
read.note: In German. Cool, dry, dark and locked away from children, not in the bathroom; a yearly check; old medicines back to the pharmacy.

choices.label: Fear, stress or grief after a disaster
choices.hint: Can't sleep, worried all the time, someone in shock or despair

read.label: What helps with fear and worry
read.note: In German. Keeping in touch, daily routines, going outside, rest, and only as much news as you need. German helplines.

read.label: Psychological first aid: look, listen, link
read.note: How to approach and listen to someone in distress, and what not to say.

read.label: Ways to calm yourself
read.note: In German. Slow breathing, small tasks, a blanket, moving about, keeping a diary.

read.label: When to get specialist help
read.note: No sleep for a week, unable to cope with daily life, or threatening to harm themselves or others.

read.label: How children may react
read.note: In German. Reactions differ; drawing and play; when to ask for advice.

read.label: Supporting a child
read.note: In German. Listen, answer honestly and simply, do not force a talk, reassure.

choices.label: Someone needs extra care
choices.hint: A disability, hearing or sight loss, an older person living alone

read.label: Preparing with an impairment
read.note: In German. Aids, spare batteries and chargers, a medicines plan, an assistance animal, contacts.

read.label: Talking with rescuers
read.note: In German. An emergency card, pen and paper, and neighbours who know how to help.

read.label: Neighbours who need help
read.note: In German. People whom carers or meal services no longer reach in a blackout.

choices.label: What goes in a first aid kit
choices.hint: For the home and the car

read.label: A household first aid kit
read.note: In German. The items an Austrian standard kit holds.

limits.text: Do not keep medicines in the bathroom, and do not flush old medicines down the toilet.
If someone does not want help, do not force it on them.
Get specialist help if a person has not slept for a week, cannot cope with daily life, or threatens to harm themselves or others.
A single debriefing session after a traumatic event may do harm.
Do not push a child to talk about the crisis.
If you are very worried about a child, ask a paediatrician, a counselling service or a child psychotherapist.
